recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not add duplicate text to references.html unless the work group later wants a separate parser algorithm statement there; the current source already conveys the implementer rule needed to avoid the FHIR-23011 ambiguity.
issue_request: FHIR-23011 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-I change request for R5 asking that canonical reference URL parsing be made unambiguous when a canonical resource version contains '#'. The resolution required guidance that conformance/canonical resource versions SHOULD NOT contain '#', because parsers presume an unescaped hash starts a fragment id and embedded hashes in versions create parsing failure.
initial_application: Git commit 6052da613c, titled "FHIR-23011 Parsing of canonical reference urls is ambiguous", applied the issue by adding a Business Version note to source/resource/resource-notes.xml and appending '#'-avoidance comments to canonical-resource version elements. Current source still carries that application.
additional_context: The linked Zulip thread confirms the ambiguity between http://fhir.acme.com/Questionnaire/example|1.0#vs1 and a version value such as 2019#1. A later applied issue, FHIR-47736, concerned a separate Requirements statement-link use of '#' with canonical URLs and resolved by changing the Requirements model, not by superseding the FHIR-23011 guidance. No Confluence reference for FHIR-23011 was found.
reconciliation: No source change was made. source/resource/resource-notes.xml already says canonical-resource business versions SHOULD NOT contain '#', explains that '#' has special URL meaning, and requires escaping if used in a version inside a URL. source/canonicalresource/structuredefinition-CanonicalResource.xml links CanonicalResource.version to that shared note, and matching comments appear across canonical resource version definitions.

related_jiras.note: Later Applied issue about '#' in Requirements statement links confirmed the same canonical URL character concern but changed the Requirements model rather than superseding FHIR-23011 guidance.
